chunks: And from him (Al-Ukhu) from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

A man ordered a man to marry him a woman from the people of Basra from the tribe of Banu Tamim, so he married him a woman from the people of Kufa from the tribe of Banu Tamim. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He differed from his order; upon the one commanded (the matchmaker) is half the dowry for the family of the wife, and there is no waiting period for her, and there is no inheritance between them.'

He said, and some of those present said to him: 'If he ordered him to marry him a woman and did not specify a place or a tribe, and then the commander denied that he had ordered him with that after he had married him, he said: 'If the one commanded has evidence that he had ordered him to marry him, then the dowry is upon the commander for the family of the wife, and if he does not have evidence, then the dowry is upon the one commanded for the family of the wife, and there is no inheritance between them and no waiting period.'
And she has half the dowry if he had stipulated a dowry for her, and if he did not specify a dowry for her, then she has nothing.'

key_terms.آمِر: The commander/one who gives the order

ai.seo_question: What is the financial liability of a matchmaker if he marries a man to a woman different from the specified location or tribe?
ai.summary: From *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the principles of agency (*wakalah*) in marriage contracts, distinguishing between specific and general mandates. It establishes that deviation from explicit instructions (place/tribe) imposes half the dowry on the agent with no inheritance, while ambiguity in the mandate shifts the financial burden based on the validity of the agent's proof against the principal's denial. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on precise contractual terms and the equitable distribution of dowry (*mahr*) liabilities in cases of disputed agency.
